native_result.query: In which century do Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends for the first time, with Pottery Decoration increasing significantly and Pottery Form declining simultaneously?
native_result.HypoA: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline. This marks a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.
native_result.HypoB: The first century in which Diversity in Pottery Decoration rises significantly while Diversity in Pottery Form simultaneously declines is the 17th century BCE (CE = -1700): Decoration jumps from Z=-0.48 to Z=+0.97 (Δ=+1.45) while Form collapses from Z=+0.74 to Z=-1.13 (Δ=-1.87). This is the only reverse-growth event in the series (CE -4100 to -500) and is robust to all thresholds (0.05-0.5 Z units), quantile-based thresholds (50th-90th percentile), interpolated columns, and 100-year smoothing.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded time_series_data.csv (3601 annual rows, CE -4100..-500); extracted the 37 century-resolution raw Z values for PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration. 2) Cross-validated against capital.csv: 37/39 rows match exactly under BCE=-CE; the BCE 4300 and 4200 rows are backfilled duplicates of CE -4100 and were excluded from chronological scanning. 3) Computed per-century deltas (dForm, dDeco); defined reverse growth as dDeco >= +thr AND dForm <= -thr; scanned chronologically from the CE -4100 anchor for the first occurrence. 4) Sensitivity: threshold sweep 0.05-0.5, quantile thresholds (50/75/90 pct of |dDeco|), _inter column century deltas, and 100-year rolling-mean smoothing — all yield CE -1700. Pollen openness data used only as background context.

sub_hypo.text: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline, marking a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.
sub_hypo.context: In 1700 BCE, with this divergence occurring for the first time.
sub_hypo.relations: Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases significantly while Diversity in Pottery Form declines notably, producing a unique divergence in their growth trends.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline. This marks a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.

sub_hypo.text: The first and only century in which Pottery Decoration diversity rises significantly while Pottery Form diversity simultaneously declines is the 17th century BCE (CE = -1700). Decoration rises from Z = -0.48 to +0.97 (Δ = +1.45), while Form falls from Z = +0.74 to -1.13 (Δ = -1.87).
sub_hypo.context: Chronological scanning of 37 century-resolution raw archaeological Z values from CE -4100 to -500, cross-validated against capital.csv using BCE = -CE; backfilled duplicate rows at BCE 4300 and 4200 are excluded.
sub_hypo.relations: Reverse growth requires simultaneous per-century changes dDecoration >= +threshold and dForm <= -threshold. CE -1700 is the first and only such event in the series, with changes of +1.45 and -1.87 Z units, respectively.

sub_hypo.text: Identification of CE -1700 as the reverse-growth event is robust to thresholds of 0.05–0.5 Z units, quantile-based thresholds, interpolated columns, and 100-year smoothing.
sub_hypo.context: Sensitivity analysis of the CE -4100 to -500 archaeological series using fixed thresholds of 0.05–0.5 Z units, the 50th, 75th, and 90th percentiles of absolute per-century Decoration changes, interpolated-column century deltas, and 100-year rolling means.
sub_hypo.relations: All tested threshold and preprocessing variants identify CE -1700 as the first simultaneous Decoration increase and Form decrease satisfying dDecoration >= +threshold and dForm <= -threshold.

This is the only reverse-growth event in the series (CE -4100 to -500) and is robust to all thresholds (0.05-0.5 Z units), quantile-based thresholds (50th-90th percentile), interpolated columns, and 100-year smoothing.
